verdict.rationale: The evidence shows no official three.js language server and no first-party typed API definitions. TypeScript typings come from the community @types/three package, which the maintainer explicitly declines to maintain and whose signatures sometimes drift from the code. That makes it a third-party workaround, not the product's own capability. The 'type-safe' TSL claim concerns shader-node composition, which is an adjacent feature and not editor tooling for completions, diagnostics or navigation.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, the scripting language has first-class machine tooling — an official language server (LSP) or typed API definitions a coding agent's editor can attach to for completions, diagnostics, and navigation

citations.quote: there are some function signatures that don't match what's in the code using @types/three, and mrdoob does not want to maintain this
three.js works flawlessly with Typescript too
